_meta.note: Captured off the wire from `dsh --profile acp` with Kiro Crew's gate plugin (src/kiro_crew/agent_sdk/gate_extensions/deepseek/kiro_crew_tool_gate.mjs) composed through the per-launch `--patch` file the client writes. This is the frame class #10373 could not capture and had to synthesize: with the plugin loaded the harness DOES ask, because the plugin answers dsh's own `tools/pre-execute` waterfall with `{kind: 'ask'}` and dsh's tools core resolves that through `ctx.approval`, which the ACP bridge answers by emitting session/request_permission. Three frames, in wire order, because the correlation between them is the point: this harness's permission frame carries ONLY `toolCall.toolCallId` -- no title, kind, status or rawInput -- so the tool identity and arguments Kiro Crew's gate judges come from the `tool_call` update immediately before it, which is exactly the toolCallId-keyed cache _dispatch.build_permission_event already reads. The third frame is the same call completing after the client answered allow-once, so the fixture also shows the gate releasing rather than only blocking. Two control runs were taken beside this one and are what make the plugin the cause rather than a coincidence: the SAME prompt with the plugin not composed produced no permission frame and ran the command anyway, and the same prompt answered reject-once produced the frame and left the call `failed` with `Error: the user rejected tool "bash"`, the command never run. Driven by a model served locally on loopback (an Anthropic Messages responder scripted to emit one `bash` tool_use block), so no provider credential was involved -- the same way this corpus's other live captures were driven. Agent-to-client lines are verbatim except the session id and the per-message messageId, which the agent mints and which are replaced with fixed synthetic values deliberately not uuid-shaped, so the repository's own host-data gate cannot mistake one for a leaked run id.
